children: ICE canola futures are posting solid gains Monday morning, taking back Friday's losses to start the week.
The November contract was up C$10.89 at C$833.10 per tonne, holding well above its 20-day moving average of C$820.80 with chart-based positioning a feature.
Gains in Chicago soybeans provided spillover support, with European rapeseed and Malaysian palm oil also firmer in early trade. However, Chicago soyoil held near unchanged and crude oil was lower.

The slow harvest pace in parts of Western Canada provided support, although forecasts calling for relatively warm and dry conditions for most of the Prairies over the next week should allow for good progress.
About 15,500 canola contracts had traded as of 9:46 a.m. ET.
